filename: SMLFire1.0_ a stochastic machine learning (SML) model for wildfire activity in the western United States.pdf
title: SMLFire1.0: a stochastic machine learning (SML) model for wildfire activity in the western United States
processes: wildfire burned area and size distribution
fuel moisture and fire weather dynamics
parameterization_target: subgrid wildfire frequency and burned area / fire size distributions
code_availability: The code for training and validating the SMLFire1.0 model, as well as reproducing the figures shown in this paper, is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7277980 (Buch et al., 2022). The WUMI dataset (Juang et al., 2022) contains all the fire occurrences and sizes analyzed in this paper and is hosted at https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.sf7m0cg72 (Juang and Williams, 2022).
testbed_rationale: The study provides fully public model code on Zenodo and an open dataset of historical wildfires on Dryad, designed explicitly to serve as a subgrid parameterization for fire modules in dynamic global vegetation models and Earth system models.
pain_points: Severe data class imbalance: non-fire grid cells vastly outnumber cells with observed fires (~10 million vs ~17,500), requiring downsampling and spline calibration to curb false positives.
Heavy-tailed extreme value distributions: lognormal distributions underpredict extremes; generalized Pareto distributions with infinite variance are required.
Nonstationarity and regime shift: fire size responses shifted drastically post-2004, requiring a manual breakpoint to combine two GPD models.
Underprediction of record-breaking extreme wildfire years (e.g., 2020 forest fire sizes substantially exceeded the 1984-2019 training regime).
Data quality/reporting gaps: post-2017 federal agency reporting underrepresents smaller fires (< 4 km^2) outside California.
extraction_notes: SMLFire1.0 is targeted for subgrid parameterization inside DGVMs and ESMs, though evaluated offline in this study. The research is supported by the NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (grant no. 2019625).
